Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller films released in 2020 (in no particular order). These picks span a range of styles—from gritty neo‑noir to high‑stakes heist dramas—and have received praise from critics and audiences alike.

| # | Title | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | A sprawling, time‑juggling saga that blends historical crime with Scorsese’s signature storytelling. |
| 2 | **Uncut Gems** | Josh and Benny Safdie | Adam Sandler, Jennifer Lawrence | Sandler’s frenetic performance anchors a tense, pulse‑pounding narrative about risk and obsession. |
| 3 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Ewan McGregor, Sacha Baron Cohen | A courtroom thriller that mixes real events with sharp dialogue and a strong ensemble cast. |
| 4 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie’s slick direction and witty script make this a stylish, fast‑paced caper. |
| 5 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A psychological thriller that examines paranoia and social media’s impact on identity. |
| 6 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern take on the classic horror‑thriller hybrid, blending suspense with social commentary. |
| 7 | **The Nightingale** | Jennifer Kent | Lily James, David Wenham | A visceral, atmospheric thriller set in 19th‑century Tasmania, exploring revenge and colonial brutality. |
| 8 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A medieval crime‑thriller that reimagines a historical duel as a courtroom drama. |
| 9 | **The Platform** | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Iván Massagué, Zorion Eguileor | A dystopian thriller that uses a vertical prison setting to explore class conflict. |
|10 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern take on the classic horror‑thriller hybrid, blending suspense with social commentary. |

### How to Watch

- **Streaming**: Many of these titles are available on major platforms such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu, and HBO Max.  
- **Rent/Buy**: Digital rental or purchase options are typically available on iTunes, Google Play, and YouTube Movies.  
- **Physical Media**: Blu‑ray/DVD releases can be found on Amazon or local retailers.

Enjoy your binge‑watching!
